newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD says U.S. delays granting of phone licence.
newsitem.headline: KDD says U.S. delays granting of phone licence.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd said on Wednesday that the U.S. Federal Communications Commission had informed KDD's U.S. unit that the granting of a U.S. licence to provide international phone services would be delayed.

The FCC informed the KDD unit in a letter on March 7 that KDD would be excluded from a simplified application procedure for U.S. licences, under which companies seeking U.S. phone licences would be automatically granted permission within 35 days of application, a KDD spokesman said.
The FCC said the United States Trade Representative, the U.S. Department of Commerce and the U.S. State Department had made requests that KDD be excluded from the simplified application procedure.
No further details were given on the reason of why the U.S. authorities made the request, the spokesman said.
Asked if the decision was made in retaliation for Japan's rejection of a U.S. demand to remove a foreign ownership ratio on telecommunication companies, the spokesman said: "We simply have no idea."
Foreign investors are currently only permitted to hold up to 20 percent of shares in KDD and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT).
